body:
Track robofab, follow-up to `robofab-cell-cv`. Tests whether adding load/unload time to the printer demand improves MVA of the robot-printer cell. Result is mixed: better at saturation (2.9% vs 8.2% mean abs error), worse elsewhere (7.3% vs 3.6%), worse overall (6.2% vs 4.7%). Stylised, simulation-only. 5 tests pass; `python site/build.py` prints ok.

comments.body:
When a print finishes before the warm-up boundary but its unload starts afterward, this includes the pre-warm-up portion of the wait even though the denominator covers only `horizon - warmup`. Clamp the wait start to `warmup` so the reported stall share measures the documented interval.

This issue also appears on line 100 of the same file.

@@ -0,0 +1,110 @@
+"""Discrete-event simulation of the same cell, with switches that remove or add one departure from
+product form at a time. Copied from research/robofab-cell-mva (same author, MIT) so this project is self-contained, then
+instrumented: ``simulate(..., stats=True)`` also returns the share of printer-time spent finished but
+waiting for the arm to unload ("stall"), which `robofab-cell-mva` only conjectured.
+
+mode "pf" (product-form-compatible): per pass the arm does one service (load + unload together),
+then the job takes a printer for the print time only, then an inspection station.
+mode "hold": the real cell semantics: a printer is seized at the start of the load and released at
+the end of the unload; the arm does load and unload as separate FIFO services.
+dist: "exp" (exponential), "det" (deterministic) or "ln" (lognormal, coefficient of variation cv).
+"""
+import heapq, math
+import numpy as np
+
+
+def _draw(rng, mean, dist, cv):
+    if dist == "det":
+        return mean
+    if dist == "exp":
+        return rng.exponential(mean)
+    s2 = math.log(1 + cv * cv)
+    return mean * math.exp(rng.normal(-s2 / 2, math.sqrt(s2)))
+
+
+def simulate(types, printers, inspectors, wip, mode="pf", dist="exp", cv=0.3,
+             horizon=24 * 60.0, warmup=4 * 60.0, seed=0, stats=False):
+    """Good parts per minute after warm-up. ``types`` as in mva.cell_demands (equal mix by weight)."""
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    w = np.array([t["weight"] for t in types], float); w /= w.sum()
+    ev, seq = [], 0
+    def push(t, kind, j):
+        nonlocal seq
+        seq += 1
+        heapq.heappush(ev, (t, seq, kind, j))
+    typ = {}
+    jid = 0
+    q_arm, q_prn, q_ins = [], [], []
+    arm_busy, free_p, free_i = False, printers, inspectors
+    done = 0
+    pe, stall = {}, 0.0      # print-end time per job; accumulated printer stall after warm-up
+
+    def new_job():
+        nonlocal jid
+        jid += 1
+        typ[jid] = types[rng.choice(len(types), p=w)]
+        q_arm.append((jid, "both" if mode == "pf" else "load"))     # first step of a pass
+
+    def start(now):
+        nonlocal arm_busy, free_p, free_i, stall
+        while free_i > 0 and q_ins:
+            j = q_ins.pop(0); free_i -= 1
+            push(now + _draw(rng, typ[j]["inspect"], dist, cv), "ins_done", j)
+        if mode == "pf":
+            while free_p > 0 and q_prn:
+                j = q_prn.pop(0); free_p -= 1
+                push(now + _draw(rng, typ[j]["print"], dist, cv), "print_done", j)
+        if not arm_busy and q_arm:
+            # FIFO among eligible entries: unloads, or loads when a printer is free
+            k = next((i for i, a in enumerate(q_arm) if a[1] == "unload" or mode == "pf" or free_p > 0), None)
+            if k is not None:
+                if mode == "hold" and q_arm[k][1] == "load":
+                    free_p -= 1          # the printer is seized when the load starts
+                j, op = q_arm.pop(k)
+                if op == "unload" and now >= warmup:
+                    stall += now - pe[j]

comments.body:
The simulator's `horizon=24*60` is measured from time zero and the rate denominator is `horizon - warmup`, so these runs have a 24-hour total horizon with a 20-hour observation window—not a 24-hour horizon after warm-up. Correct this for reproducibility.

This issue also appears on line 35 of the same file.

@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+# Does holding the printer through load and unload fix mean value analysis of a robot-printer cell? A mixed result
+
+A stylised, simulation-only follow-up to `research/robofab-cell-cv` (track `robofab`, milestone 4's next steps). That project's accounting suggested that most of mean value analysis' (MVA) overshoot at saturation comes from the printer being held through the arm's load and unload. The obvious analytic repair is to add load and unload time to the printer's service demand (`cell_demands(..., hold_printer=True)`). Here I test it as a predictor against the discrete-event simulation, in 32 settings. All numbers are from `experiments/results.txt` (20 seeds, 24 h horizon after a 4 h warm-up, mean rates in good parts per hour). Job types and times are those of `robofab-cell-mva` (A: 20 min print, 10% fail; B: 60 min print, 20% fail; load and unload 2 min; inspect 3 min; equal mix), illustrative and not measured.
